entry.title: Social Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
Launch of the week — Bot Screen / desktop passthrough in Hermes Desktop: The official NousResearch announcement of Bot Screen (real-time streaming of any agent's browser or terminal session) was the top post of the batch, with Teknium's companion reveal of the interactive desktop passthrough — visually and interactively accessing the same machine your Hermes Agent works on — pulling 1,148+ likes. @tonbistudio's walkthrough video and docs were amplified by both NousResearch (544 likes, ~46k views) and Teknium, making this feature the undisputed center of attention.

Community OSS — oh-my-hermes & Jev ecosystem: rlaope open-sourced jeval (Jev evaluation/visualization) and shipped oh-my-hermes support for Jev-Skills and model routing (Jev models/aliases, skills/plugins, workflows), positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for hermes-agent power users — the strongest original-contribution thread of the period.

Maintainer engagement & official support: Teknium directly rebutted a reported cache problem (demanding reproducible issue-tracker paths, signaling thorough testing) and confirmed a rapid fix, while NousResearch dispensed a practical usage tip (Hermes via iMessage with any model, 121 likes) and Teknium corrected a public misattribution, clarifying the work in question is built by Nous Research, not Anthropic.

Sentiment: Overwhelmingly positive and long-awaited — Teknium's "Much needed!" (202 likes, ~20k views) and "Impressive!" endorsement captured launch enthusiasm. Remaining posts (emoji-only replies, bare link reposts, engagement-bait prompts, vague Opus 5.5/Claude Code takes) carried little informational value and were excluded from the ranking.
